title: Agent Pay Level 1 purchase with edge verification
summary: A registered agent signs its web requests with RFC 9421 and the tag Agent-pay-auth. The CDN or merchant runs Mastercard's checklist (tag, fields, timestamps, an 8-minute window and the nonce first, then the key from Mastercard's key directory and the signature), the agent types its agentic token into the normal card form, and the authorization runs over the existing card rails. Mastercard publishes no wire schema for the network leg.

steps.label: Signed GET with tag Agent-pay-auth
steps.detail: The agent signs each request with HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421). Signature-Input covers @authority and @path and carries keyid, alg, created, expires, nonce and the tag. Mastercard's guide gives the Mastercard tag as Agent-pay-auth; its testing glossary writes agent-pay-auth. The guide's example Signature-Agent host does not resolve, so this example uses a placeholder host, and keyid and signature are placeholders.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, Agent Pay developer guides as read 2026-10-21. Placeholder values; the signature does not verify.
GET /product/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: shop.example.com
Signature-Agent: "https://agent-keys.example.com/"
Signature-Input: sig1=("@authority" "@path");created=1791720000;expires=1791720480;keyid="<key-thumbprint>";alg="ed25519";nonce="<random-nonce>";tag="Agent-pay-auth"
Signature: sig1=:<signature>:

failures.condition: No Signature-Input with a scheme tag
failures.outcome: Treat as an ordinary bot and apply the non-agent bot policy

steps.label: Check tag, fields, timestamps and nonce
steps.detail: Mastercard's checklist comes first: a scheme tag, every required field including @authority and @path, created in the past, expires in the future, no more than 8 minutes between created and expires, and a nonce not seen in the last 8 minutes.

failures.condition: created in the future, expires in the past, or a window longer than 8 minutes
Nonce seen in the last 8 minutes

steps.label: Fetch key for keyid, verify signature
steps.detail: Only then does the verifier look up the agent key named by keyid in Mastercard's key directory, rebuild the signature base from the covered components, verify the signature and record the nonce with its expiry. Cloudflare said in 2025-10 that each network will host its own directory and names no Mastercard URL; the directory location is not public.

failures.condition: Key not found in the directory

steps.label: Forward as a trusted agent
steps.detail: The edge passes the request to the merchant site, which can now serve the agent instead of challenging it as a bot.

steps.label: Fill card form with agentic token
steps.detail: The agent types the agentic token into the standard card number, expiry and security code fields. The token looks like a card number to the merchant, so PCI scope does not change. Agents may not use a card already on file at the merchant, because the network could not then see the flow as agentic.

failures.condition: Agent uses a card on file instead of an agentic token
failures.outcome: The network cannot recognize the transaction as agentic

steps.label: Submit authorization
steps.detail: The merchant processes the payment through its existing acquirer or PSP, as for any card-not-present payment.

steps.label: Authorization request
steps.detail: The network detokenizes and checks the token limits. Stripe says agentic network tokens map to the latest funding PAN and include additional information in the authorization message for issuers; neither Stripe nor Mastercard names a data element for it.

failures.condition: Token used outside its merchant, amount or time limits

steps.label: Route to issuer
steps.detail: The issuer makes the final approve or decline decision with the additional information it receives.

steps.label: Approve or decline
steps.detail: The response returns through network and acquirer. Standard chargeback rights apply afterwards; no agent-specific reason code was found in public, and the Mastercard Rules point Agent Pay participants to Program Standards that are not public.
